issues.issue: Original printed Chapter CIII / sequential editorial CIV begins first-edition PDF559/printed525 and ends above the distinct printed CHAP CIV heading on PDF561/printed527.
The subject is infant survival and length of life, a high-stakes historical astrology belief; extracted source rules are NOT medical prognosis or validated survival science.
No identified infant, birth certificate, long-term survival cohort, deaths, parental charts or independently verified observed outcomes accompany this passage.
Historical terms 'long life', 'short life', 'past infancy', 'may live long', 'hardly escapes infancy' and 'old age' have no numerical thresholds or calibrated survival probabilities.
Five hylegical places and the lord of geniture allow multiple possible significators; selecting which one applies can change alleged risk.
The text treats planets as causes of health, moisture, dryness and death, but these are unverified seventeenth-century medical/astrological assumptions.
Source explicitly invokes parental nativities and children significators; no independent hereditary or medical validity is established for charts of parents.
Exact stellar and planetary aspects, rising degree, house placements, dignity and malefic contacts require reproducible period ephemeris/house calculations not provided in this batch.
Source uses 'extremely afflicted', 'well dignified', 'small sickness', 'malevolent', 'violent fixed stars' and similar unquantified magnitude conditions without objective cutoffs.
Source's infant-survival assumptions conflate chart features with unmeasured selection, seasonality, prematurity and clinical circumstances.

Lunar birth phases are given mostly unfavorable moisture/dryness associations, while an ancient-author exception for exact Sun/Moon conjunction or opposition plus benefic Ascendant gives a favorable but shorter-than-old-age result; preserve both branches.
Claims concerning new-moon/full-moon mortality or infant size are not grounded in clinical newborn evidence.
Combustion, retrogradation and swift motion of ascendant ruler are conjunct conditions with no empirical outcome data.
Source distinguishes Sun as luminary of day and Moon as luminary of night; do not pool without preserving diurnal/nocturnal status.
Author attributes one Ascendant-ruler judgment to Schoner and an exception to 'the Ancients'; their independent original documents have not been audited.
Planetary dignities in specific houses and benefic/malefic rulership are historical source classifications, not physical effects.
Source's Mars-in-Aries and Saturn-in-Capricorn danger claims depend jointly on horizon placement and diurnal/nocturnal status, not simple sign placement.
References to eighth-house, sixth and twelfth placement may reflect selective outcome framing rather than independent risk.
The fourth-house Moon aspect used to allege difficult labor is not evidence of obstetrical complications or subsequent infant survival.
The author says NOT to pronounce death rashly and to examine all significators; this is a qualification, not validation or an acceptable clinical prediction workflow.
Promised directed timing from luminary to a malefic is not independently verified by dated events and must be separated from static chart associations.
The conjunction/planet besiegement arguments on PDF561 may have multiple overlapping conditions; source annotations are not independent prediction samples.
The opening Hyleg/Apheta/killing-planet definitions following the divider on PDF561 are separate following-chapter navigation only.
All original PDF559–561 scans are independently SHA256 retained; original visual witness coverage is complete but no second full diplomatic transcription has been carried out.
No clinical, natal survival predictive validation or approved runtime model promotion has occurred.
